Four electric guitars, each with its real control layout. Pick any two, set one, and translate the setting to the other. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Learn how a magnetic pickup hears a string, and why its place on the string matters.
2. Hear single coils and humbuckers, in-between positions and the tone and volume knobs.
3. Translate a sound from one guitar to another and read what is lost.
:::

## How a pickup hears a string

- A pickup is a magnet inside a coil of wire. The steel string moving over it makes a small voltage in the coil. The pickup hears how fast the string moves at that one spot.
- A plucked string sounds many harmonics at once. Each harmonic has still points (nodes) along the string. A pickup sitting on a node does not hear that harmonic. So a pickup's place makes a **comb filter**: some harmonics strong, some missing (Tillman, 2002). Near the bridge it hears more high harmonics: brighter. Further away: warmer.
- A pickup is not a point: it averages the string over its width, which softens the highest harmonics. A humbucker (two coils) is wider than a single coil (Tillman, 2002).
- The coil's wire (its **inductance**) and the capacitance of the coil and the cable make a **resonance**, a small peak in the treble. More turns of wire: a lower peak (Wikipedia, "Pickup (music technology)"); with a normal cable most pickups peak between about 2 and 5 kHz (Lemme).
- The **tone knob** joins a capacitor to the signal through a variable resistor: turned down, it lowers and flattens the peak. The **volume knob** turned part way puts resistance in front of the cable's capacitance, so some treble is lost as well as level.
- Two pickups together add their combs; some harmonics cancel: the Strat's in-between "quack". Wired out of phase they subtract: the low harmonics cancel, a thin, nasal sound.
- Single coils pick up mains hum; a humbucker's two coils get opposite hum and cancel it (Wikipedia, "Pickup (music technology)").

## The guitars side by side

Choose a guitar for each side. Click a selector, drag a knob (arrow keys work too) and press a ▶ button. The picture shows the harmonics of the open A string at the jack (bars) and the circuit alone (line). **Amp** sends the sound through the site's amp model (the one on [Gear 3](gear-amps.qmd)); **Strings: Band samples** plays the band's guitar samples through the circuit only (the samples already went through a pickup, so the place on the string is not changed). The ☀ / ☾ button switches every panel between a white and a black background.

```{=html}
<div class="gtc" data-a="strat" data-b="lespaul"></div>
```

## Translating between guitars

**Translate** finds the setting on the other guitar that sounds most like this one: it tries every switch position and tone setting and compares the share of sound in third-octave bands for three open strings. The report says:

- **exact**: the same kind of pickups in the same places, and almost the same sound;
- **approx**: the closest setting, with notes on what differs (for example, a Strat's middle pickup on a Les Paul, which has none);
- **lost**: nothing comes close.

Try the Strat's position 2 to the Les Paul, or the Les Paul's out-of-phase what-if to the Strat.

## What is this site's own

- The string model, the pickup and pot values, the knob curves and every pickup distance except the Strat's are this site's estimates (marked unverified in the code, `apps/shared/lessons/guitar-pickups.js`). The Strat's distances are Tillman's.
- The drawings are after photos, not measured drawings; no makers' logos.
- Nobody has compared the sound with real guitars.

"Fender Telecaster." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_Telecaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_Telecaster). Broadcaster 1950, two single coils, bridge wound hotter, 1967 wiring neck / both / bridge, 25.5 in.

"Gibson Les Paul." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibson_Les_Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibson_Les_Paul). 1952; Seth Lover's humbuckers on Les Pauls from 1957; two volume, two tone, three-way; 24.75 in; Knopfler 1958 on Money for Nothing, Lukather 1959 in the Rosanna video.

"Gibson SG." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibson_SG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibson_SG). 1961; a volume and tone per pickup; three-way; 24.75 in; Angus Young, Tony Iommi's 1964 SG Special on the early albums.

Lemme, Helmuth E. W. "The Secrets of Electric Guitar Pickups." [buildyourguitar.com/resources/lemme/](https://buildyourguitar.com/resources/lemme/). Resonance of most pickups with a normal cable 2,000-5,000 Hz; inductance 1-10 H (not read directly: certificate expired 2026-11-26; unverified).

"Pickup (music technology)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickup_(music_technology)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickup_(music_technology)). Single coils pick up hum; humbucker coils cancel it; self-capacitance + cable resonate with the inductance; more turns, lower resonance.

Tillman, J. Donald. "Response Effects of Guitar Pickup Position and Width." 2000, updated 17 Oct. 2002. [www.till.com/articles/PickupResponse/index.html](https://www.till.com/articles/PickupResponse/index.html). Pickup point response sin(pi x F / (L F0)) = a comb filter; aperture term; Strat neck / middle / bridge 6.375 / 3.875 / 1.625 in, 1 in aperture; humbucker about 2.5 in; out-of-phase cancellation.
